note: Am7, Dsus2 and Dm7 as open shapes, then strummed in time with the island strum. The open shapes are the lesson, so only the tempo moves (80 to 100 bpm); the why names the two notes the sus2 and the m7 share, and the listening line says what to listen for, not how it sounds.

exercise.title: Am7, Dsus2, Dm7
exercise.why: Dsus2 and Dm7 share their two lowest notes, so moving from one to the other changes only the top of the chord.

cells.text:
Press a chord box below to hear it, then fret each chord as shown. Change from Dsus2 to Dm7 and back, then add Am7 in front.
Practice until the fingers on the top two strings move together, as one.

Press Play below to start the metronome at {{=bpm}}. After a bar of count-in, the lit box shows the chord to play: Am7 for two bars, then Dsus2 and Dm7 for a bar each. Strum the pattern shown in the boxes.
Listen for the top note that moves when Dsus2 changes to Dm7.
